verdict.rationale: Weave's first-party docs describe custom scorers for encoding use-case-specific evaluation criteria. They can be function-based (`@weave.op`-decorated Python functions) or class-based (inheriting from `weave.Scorer`), and they return a dictionary of metric results that plugs into the `Evaluation` object. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that custom code scorers work as documented.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can write custom code-based scorers and metrics for my evaluations

citations.quote: Custom Scorers let you encode evaluation criteria that are specific to your use case, beyond what the built-in Scorers cover.
Function-based Scorers: Python functions decorated with @weave.op. Class-based Scorers: Python classes that inherit from weave.Scorer for more complex evaluations.
In Weave, Scorers evaluate AI outputs and return evaluation metrics. They take the AI’s output, analyze it, and return a dictionary of results.
